articles.title: Källor: Astra Zeneca har lagt mångmiljardbud i USA
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Källor: Astra Zeneca har lagt mångmiljardbud i USA
articles.body_text: Källor: Astra Zeneca har lagt mångmiljardbud i USA Läkemedelskoncernen Astra Zeneca har lagt ett bud på motsvarande 97 miljarder kronor på det USA-noterade bolaget Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, uppger källor för Wall Street Journal (WSJ) . Enligt uppgifterna lade Astra Zeneca budet på 10 miljarder dollar i oktober. Det innebär en betalning på 124 dollar per aktie i Rhythm – som specialiserar sig på behandlingar för metabola sjukdomar och svår fetma. Sedan uppgifterna om budet blev omskrivna steg Rhytms aktiekurs 28 procent på onsdagen, till knappt 111 dollar. Ett köp skulle utöka Astra Zenecas portfölj av behandlingar mot sällsynta sjukdomar.

articles.title: Google stänger av AI-funktion i klassrummet
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Google stänger av AI-funktion i klassrummet
articles.body_text: Google döms till miljardböter. Arkivbild. Google stänger av AI-funktion i klassrummet Google kommer att stänga av sina AI-verktyg som standard för skolbarn. Ändringen kommer först att rullas ut i USA – för att senare börja gälla i hela världen. Beskedet kommer efter hård kritik om att företaget har ”tvingat på” elever AI-funktioner, trots att det fortfarande pågår en debatt om hur tekniken bör användas i klassrummen. Google dominerar teknikutbudet i amerikanska skolor. Appar som Gmail, Docs, plattformen Classroom och Search används dagligen i klassrum över hela landet. Dessutom är företagets Chromebook den dator som skolorna oftast tillhandahåller sina elever. På tisdagen presenterade Google ändringen som innebär att Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom och Search ska vara avstängda för elever som går i grundskolan och gymnasiet, till dess en skoladministratör slår på dem. Sökmotorjätten uppger för AFP att USA är först ut. I ett nästa steg kommer den att införas världen över. Det finns dock inte något datum. Ändringen innebär också att skolor inte kommer att kunna ge elever tillgång till Search utan dess AI-funktioner. Chris Phillips, chef för Googles utbildningsverksamhet, säger till The New York Times att "Search och AI är djupt integrerade”, eftersom AI-funktioner nu är inbyggda i företagets sökmotor. En av dem som riktat skarp kritik mot Google är New Yorks nye borgmästare Zohran Mamdani. På X har han anklagat företaget för att ”försöka använda sin monopolställning för att tvinga på allmänna skolor AI”. ”Inget företag borde ha makten att diktera hur vi utbildar våra barn”, skrev han.

articles.title: Försvarsjätten Rheinmetall vinstvarnar
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Försvarsjätten Rheinmetall vinstvarnar
articles.body_text: Vapentillverkare går plus runtom i världen. Arkivbild. För andra gången i år släpper den tyska försvarsbolaget Rheinmetall en vinstvarning för helåret. Orsaken är förseningar i ett program för pansarfordon. Enligt ett pressmeddelande på onsdagen räknar bolaget nu med en försäljning på cirka 13,2 miljarder euro (drygt 144 miljarder kronor) i år, en sänkning från det tidigare intervallet på 13,7–14,2 miljarder euro. Förseningarna i programmet för pansarfordonet Boxer innebär att beställningar skjuts upp till nästa år. Rheinmetall sänker också prognosen för rörelsemarginalen, till 18,5 procent från den tidigare 19 procent. Även i augusti tvingades bolaget sänka sin försäljningsprognos, då tyska försvaret avbeställde sex fregatter.

articles.title: Oljepriset rasar efter Vances utspel om Iran
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Oljepriset rasar efter Vances utspel om Iran
articles.body_text: Oljepriset rasar efter Vances utspel om Iran Priset på olja faller skarpt. Det sker sedan JD Vance skyllt Republikanernas valförlust på Irankriget. ”Anledningen till att vi förlorade är kriget. Det sade presidenten själv i går kväll”, skrev Vance i ett långt inlägg på X under eftermiddagen svensk tid. I samma veva störtdök terminspriserna på råolja. Priset på Nordsjöolja (Brent) har fallit nästan nio procent under onsdagen och handlas omkring 95 dollar per fat. Amerikansk WTI-olja har fallit med nästan 8 procent, till omkring 88 dollar per fat. Enligt CNBC ser investerarna Vance uttalande som en indikation på att valresultatet kan få president Donald Trump att börja förhandla med Iran. För att kriga krävs det pengar och det är kongressen som har plånboken. Demokraternas ledare i senaten, Chuck Schumer, säger att deras mål är att avsluta kriget mot Iran och att de redan har fått med sig ”några republikaner som vill stoppa kriget”. Med tanke på valresultatet och Irans ekonomiska situation verkar en överenkommelse nu mer sannolik än osannolik, säger Ajay Parmar vid energianalytiker vid marknadsanalysföretaget ICIS.

articles.title: Klassiska cykelmärket Bianchi i rekonstruktion
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Klassiska cykelmärket Bianchi i rekonstruktion
articles.body_text: Marco Pantani på en Bianchi-cykel när det begav sig. Arkivbild från 2000. Klassiska cykelmärket Bianchi i rekonstruktion Den klassiska, svenskägda italienska cykeltillverkaren Bianchi har försatts i rekonstruktion. Bianchi ägs av den svenska koncernen Grimaldi, som genom Cycleurope även äger Crescent och Monark. Bolaget fick i förra månaden tid på sig av en italiensk domstol att ta sig ur sina ekonomiska bekymmer, enligt Bloomberg. Bianchi grundades i Milano 1885 och räknas som ett av världens äldsta cykelmärken. De är speciellt kända för sina turkosa racercyklar.

articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
articles.summary: At least 40 people were killed and another 30 may still be under the rubble after Monday's attack on a Ukrainian village, Kyiv says.
articles.body_text: A bodycam video has been released by Ukraine police which they say shows the moments between two powerful Russian bomb strikes that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and a shelter. The footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, shows residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha going to an underground shelter after the first attack on Monday. Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit. President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 30 people may still be under the rubble, as a search operation continued for the third day. Nine gliding bombs, some weighing 3,000kg, hit the village as people had gathered to get humanitarian aid, Ukraine said. The bodycam footage was released by Ukraine's national police on Wednesday. It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble. Severely damaged buildings are also seen. A voice of a military official is then heard on a two-way radio warning police on the ground of more glide bombs being launched towards Kamyshuvakha. "Quickly [go] to the shelter!" one of the police officers tells local residents, who are seen walking into the shelter - at least two floors underground. Seconds later the shelter is hit, and the recording stops. Ukraine said the shelter was near a local school, which was being used to distribute humanitarian aid. BBC Verify has confirmed the video was filmed in the same place as footage released by the Ukrainian state emergencies service DSNS showing the aftermath Monday's attack in Komyshuvakha.

articles.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
articles.summary: With Canada-US trade talks back on, Tuesday’s midterm Democratic wave puts pressure on the White House to come to a deal.
articles.body_text: It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies. "I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada". Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on. US voters cited affordability as a main concern heading into the midterms and a survey by the Cato Institute in September suggested that about 75% believe the tariffs have raised prices. In states like Maine and Michigan, tariffs played a significant role in the hard-fought races. In Maine, incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins clashed with the White House over tariffs. She successfully lobbied to have some duties that directly affected the state removed, including on road salt, refrigeration equipment and seaweed, but in the end lost to Democrat Troy Jackson. A similar story played out in Michigan, where state's the automobile manufacturing industry is deeply intertwined with Canada's - and where Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers. In Ohio, Senator-elect Sherrod Brown, who defeated Republican Jon Husted, called the levies a "disaster" and vowed to slash costs for voters by getting rid of them . Democratic leaders like Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer, now newly empowered, have both pushed to rein in the tariffs on Canada in recent months. Still, Democratic control of Congress might not do much to move the needle on tariffs. Trump's levies have been largely enacted using executive orders without approval from Congress. And speaking to Fox News on Tuesday night, Trump touted his "ultimate power" of veto to shut down bills passed by Congress that he does not like.

articles.title: Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock
articles.summary: Herzog warns politicians that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid another election.
articles.body_text: Israel's President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with political parties on whom to task with forming a new coalition government, after he received the official results of a general election last week he said had no clear winner. Herzog told party leaders that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid a new election. Neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament. Earlier, electoral officials said there was no evidence of irregularities and that unsubstantiated claims by Netanyahu's camp of Arab-led parties "stealing" the election did not justify delaying the results' certification. The Shin Bet security service is investigating allegations of foreign interference in the election, but the head of the Central Elections Committee stressed that they would not fundamentally change the outcome. In the election on 27 October, Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48. Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters. That makes them potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government. The role of Israel's president is largely ceremonial, but after an election they have the role of inviting a Knesset member to form a government. That person will be given 28 days to do so, with a potential 14-day extension. The president has wide discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition. They do not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats. On Wednesday morning, Herzog was presented with the official results by Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg at a ceremony in Jerusalem. "In recent days, we have heard voices trying to cast doubt on the election results and to undermine their legitimacy. This is a real danger," Sohlberg said.

articles.title: Hungary opens secret police files, 37 years after fall of communism
articles.summary: Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish.
articles.body_text: Hungary has opened communist-era secret police files to the public, in a controversial move the government says will help Hungarian society heal itself from the traumas of 45 years of communist rule. Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and that the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish to family members. The date of the opening is symbolic - on 4 November 1956 Soviet tanks rolled through Budapest and other cities, to crush Hungary's short-lived revolution. "I ask everyone to treat this long overdue publication of documents with dignity and humanity," Prime Minister Péter Magyar told reporters at the state archives in Budapest. "Many families will now face difficult information, often related to a deceased relative," he added. "It is impossible to process a trauma without discussion and asking questions." Magyar defended the move, which was a central promise of his election campaign ahead of his landslide victory in April elections, as the fulfilment of a promise made by those who toppled the Communist party in 1989 in Hungary. In the ensuing decades, conservative, Socialist-Liberal, and Fidesz-led governments have all contemplated, but ultimately refused to open the files. Since 1998, it has been possible to apply for your own file, and for historians to research those of others. But many names were blacked out, and many files withheld by the post-communist secret services for their own use. Over the past 36 years, there were frequent leaks of data from the files, as successive governments tried to damage their opponents. Many files were also shredded, as the Communist party lost its grip in 1988-89. From Wednesday, the names and personal data of around 60,000 people recruited by the communist-era secret services have become available on the nyitottaktak.hu website . A typical entry records the real name of the informer, their codename, date of birth, address and mother's name, their motive for recruitment - whether voluntary or because they were blackmailed or coerced - and the name of their handling officer. Another batch of files, known as the "B-dossiers" are currently being digitalised, and will be made available on 25 February.

articles.title: French blood storage impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
articles.summary: The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers.
articles.body_text: French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers. The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers, with temperatures set to rise - but staff intervened to protect blood supplies. "No health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is to be reported," the EFS said. Up until now, only supermarkets were known to have been impacted by the hacks. Meanwhile rumours have been circulating online about Russian hacktivist groups claiming they worked together to hack one of the systems that was used in the attacks which have affected European supermarkets. Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance posted that they successfully hacked Danfoss which led to speculation that they were the culprits behind the freezer hacks. But analysts now question whether or not that meant they were behind the supermarket cyber-attacks. While Russian groups are not being ruled out, experts say Iranian hacktivists or nation state hackers - or even teenagers pulling pranks - could also be the culprits. Cyber-security researchers at multiple firms are poring over evidence gathered from so-called "honeypots" to provide clues as to who is behind the waves of freezer hacks. Three separate cyber-security firms have deployed fake freezer software traps to monitor how hackers attempt to use them for attacks. In cyber-security, a "honeypot" is a digital decoy - such as a fake computer network or file - deliberately set up to look like a vulnerable target to lure and trap hackers. By monitoring these traps, security experts can safely study an attacker's methods without putting real systems at risk.

articles.title: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
articles.summary: Some Republicans tell the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost them.
articles.body_text: Inside the Republican Party, initial shock at the stunning election results on Tuesday night quickly gave way to anger with US President Donald Trump. After Democrats won upset after upset in deep-red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina, some Republicans focused their ire on Trump, arguing that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party control of Congress. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told the BBC. "This is a disaster of the first magnitude. Nobody saw it coming like this." Most Republicans expected to lose control of the House and were clear-eyed about the challenge of holding onto the Senate in a tough election cycle that favoured the party out of power. But some said in interviews that Trump dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington. "It was just one mistake after another," said Gregg Peppin, a Republican strategist in Minnesota. "Clearly, in state after state, people did not like the president's policies." A White House ally said public disapproval with Trump over the Iran war, tariffs and the administration's immigration crackdown created a "perfect storm" in November. "There's palpable frustration [within] the party about how this has all played out," the person said, and much of it is directed at Trump. Anger with Trump "is extremely high". The BBC spoke to a dozen party operatives, campaign officials, White House allies and others, many of whom spoke on background to offer a candid assessment of Trump's approach to the midterms. Trump and Republicans had a lot riding on the outcome on Tuesday night. A stronger showing by the president's party - as happened in 2022, when Democrats under then-President Joe Biden lost just nine seats in the House, and gained one in the Senate - would have given Republicans some momentum heading into 2028. But Trump will instead face a motivated Democratic majority in Congress that is eager to investigate the administration, block his judicial nominees and stymie the rest of his agenda. The midterms have ushered in an uncertain new phase in Trump's second term and may force Republicans to start grappling with their post-Trump future.

In recent weeks, Trump has warned that the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran. articles.title: Air pollution: Indian capital Delhi's air quality worsens ahead of Diwali festival
articles.summary: On Wednesday morning, Delhi's air quality index reading stood at 377, in the "very poor" category.
articles.body_text: Delhi is once again battling worsening air pollution as the onset of winter brings a familiar deterioration in air quality to India's capital. The city's air quality index (AQI) - which measures PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can clog lungs - has crossed 300, entering the "very poor" category and raising health concerns for millions of residents. Breathing such polluted air over prolonged periods can cause respiratory problems and worsen existing illnesses, with children and older people particularly vulnerable. Authorities have responded by invoking Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), introducing measures to curb dust, vehicle emissions and other sources of pollution. GRAP is a set of emergency measures that become progressively stricter as pollution levels rise. The latest restrictions include more intensive road cleaning, higher parking charges to discourage private vehicle use and increased public transport services. Delhi Metro has introduced 20 additional weekday train trips, while authorities have been directed to stagger government office timings to ease traffic congestion. Officials said the measures were introduced after forecasts suggested air quality would remain very poor over the coming days. Delhi and neighbouring parts of northern India grapple with hazardous air every winter, particularly around Diwali, one of India's biggest festivals, which is just days away. The festival is celebrated with lights, lamps and fireworks, which often worsen the city's already poor air quality by releasing fine particles and harmful gases into the atmosphere. The annual pollution crisis is driven by a combination of factors, including vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, falling temperatures, low wind speeds and the burning of crop stubble in neighbouring states. The sharp rise in pollution follows an unusually clean October, when Delhi recorded its lowest average AQI for the month in eight years. Experts have attributed the sudden deterioration to falling temperatures, slow winds and an increase in crop-residue burning in the neighbouring states of Punjab and Haryana. A recent storm had brought rain and stronger winds, helping clear the air. But as the weather settled, northwesterly winds returned, carrying smoke from burning fields towards the capital.

articles.title: South Africa local elections: ANC under pressure to reverse decline

articles.body_text: South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC). This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes. Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations. Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection. For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended. Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime. At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%. Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral. "What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday. In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support. The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard. We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?
articles.summary: Conoce el calendario oficial de feriados en Perú para 2026 y revisa qué días libres quedan en los últimos meses del año. Consulta las fechas de noviembre y diciembre para planificar tus viajes, actividades familiares o próximos descansos.
articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Fenómeno de El Niño alcanza al mango, ¿cuál es el panorama de los otros productos de la agroexportación?
articles.summary: El ministro recordó que en octubre de este año se aprobó un paquete para enfrentar el fenómeno de El Niño y los choques externos por S/18.000 millones y S/2.000 millones en otros 15 dispositivos.
articles.body_text: Las lluvias en el norte del país y las altas temperaturas están afectando a las principales frutas de exportación como el mango, confirmó el ministro de Comercio Exterior y Turismo (Mincetur), Rogers Martin Valencia. “El mango está bastante afectado. Tengo entendido que no ha habido floración. Del limón todavía no tenemos data”, explicó el ministro. Por el momento, mencionó Valencia, no se cuenta con estadísticas sobre a cuánto ascienden las pérdidas o el número de hectáreas comprometidas o en riesgo ante el fenómeno de El Niño. Según la agencia Agraria de Noticias, la Asociación Peruana de Productores y Exportadores de Mango (APEM) proyecta que las exportaciones peruanas de esta fruta fresca alcanzarían las 135.182 toneladas, representando una contracción de 39,57% frente a las 223.686 toneladas despachadas en la campaña anterior (2025/2026). En contraste, el ministro detalló que se ha logrado completar la última parte de la cosecha de uva para exportación y la carga fue embarcada sin contratiempso. “Si bien se anunciaron lluvias la semana pasada en Piura, finalmente no se registraron lluvias”, explicó. Durante la XX Cumbre Internacional de Comercio Exterior: “Cómo mantener operativo el Comercio Exterior peruano durante el fenómeno de El Niño”, organizada por la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), el ministro recordó que existe un paquete económico e instrumentos de protección diseñados para brindar certidumbre financiera y proteger a los productores y asegurar la continuidad de sus actividades. Para ello se aprobaron S/18.000 millones en aras de amortiguar los efectos directos del fenómeno de El Niño y S/2.000 millones para respaldar y financiar programas de seguros productivos y agrícolas; además de otros apoyos para el sector pesquero como la suspensión temporal del pago de cuotas de créditos otorgados a través del Fondo Nacional de Desarrollo Pesquero (Fondepes), entre otros. “Después del fenómeno hay que pensar en qué hacemos. Y eso se refleja en la articulación y la difusión de mecanismos de financiamiento de seguros, de garantías y de fondos no reembolsables, para reactivar al sector otra vez”, mencionó. De otro lado, resaltó la implementación de secuencias de cabotaje marítimo que se ha organizado para permitir el transporte de los alimentos en distintas rutas como entre los terminales de Pisco - Callao - Paita o los de Paita - Chancay - Paita, entre otros, y así evitar el desabastecimiento. “La idea es que no nos quedemos desconectados”, agregó.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. articles.title: Fenómeno de El Niño alcanza al mango, ¿cuál es el panorama de los otros productos de la agroexportación?
articles.summary: El ministro recordó que en octubre de este año se aprobó un paquete para enfrentar el fenómeno de El Niño y los choques externos por S/18.000 millones y S/2.000 millones en otros 15 dispositivos.
articles.body_text: Las lluvias en el norte del país y las altas temperaturas están afectando a las principales frutas de exportación como el mango, confirmó el ministro de Comercio Exterior y Turismo (Mincetur), Rogers Martin Valencia. “El mango está bastante afectado. Tengo entendido que no ha habido floración. Del limón todavía no tenemos data”, explicó el ministro. Por el momento, mencionó Valencia, no se cuenta con estadísticas sobre a cuánto ascienden las pérdidas o el número de hectáreas comprometidas o en riesgo ante el fenómeno de El Niño. Según la agencia Agraria de Noticias, la Asociación Peruana de Productores y Exportadores de Mango (APEM) proyecta que las exportaciones peruanas de esta fruta fresca alcanzarían las 135.182 toneladas, representando una contracción de 39,57% frente a las 223.686 toneladas despachadas en la campaña anterior (2025/2026). En contraste, el ministro detalló que se ha logrado completar la última parte de la cosecha de uva para exportación y la carga fue embarcada sin contratiempso. “Si bien se anunciaron lluvias la semana pasada en Piura, finalmente no se registraron lluvias”, explicó. Durante la XX Cumbre Internacional de Comercio Exterior: “Cómo mantener operativo el Comercio Exterior peruano durante el fenómeno de El Niño”, organizada por la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), el ministro recordó que existe un paquete económico e instrumentos de protección diseñados para brindar certidumbre financiera y proteger a los productores y asegurar la continuidad de sus actividades. Para ello se aprobaron S/18.000 millones en aras de amortiguar los efectos directos del fenómeno de El Niño y S/2.000 millones para respaldar y financiar programas de seguros productivos y agrícolas; además de otros apoyos para el sector pesquero como la suspensión temporal del pago de cuotas de créditos otorgados a través del Fondo Nacional de Desarrollo Pesquero (Fondepes), entre otros. “Después del fenómeno hay que pensar en qué hacemos. Y eso se refleja en la articulación y la difusión de mecanismos de financiamiento de seguros, de garantías y de fondos no reembolsables, para reactivar al sector otra vez”, mencionó. De otro lado, resaltó la implementación de secuencias de cabotaje marítimo que se ha organizado para permitir el transporte de los alimentos en distintas rutas como entre los terminales de Pisco - Callao - Paita o los de Paita - Chancay - Paita, entre otros, y así evitar el desabastecimiento. “La idea es que no nos quedemos desconectados”, agregó.

articles.title: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company is said to be significantly dropping the amount it's spending on AI for its engineering teams.
articles.body_text: Apple is cutting the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. It’s a big change for a company that has worked to integrate the technology into its engineering processes. In October, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for its engineering teams, decreasing it from $300 to $200, the outlet reported. And more cuts are in the works, with some allowances falling to $100 a day, sources tell Bloomberg. Outside engineering, Apple is reportedly weighing a daily limit as low as $25 a day. TechCrunch has reached out to Apple for comment. Earlier this year, a tsunami of tokenmaxxing took hold, with companies pushing staff to use AI as much as possible in the name of vaguely defined efficiency gains. The frenzy was short-lived, however, as bills for said tokens came due, and companies decided that token rationing might be a more fiscally sensible approach. Concerns persist about an apparent gap between what AI costs to build and run and the (often unclear) productivity gains the technology is suppose to generate. articles.title: After the midterms, a bigger clash over data centers could be coming | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Data center opposition crossed party lines in Tuesday’s midterms.
articles.body_text: The November 3 midterm results gave Democrats full control of Congress, setting the stage for what could be one of the most divided U.S. governments this decade, with Republicans in the White House. Tuesday’s results suggest that anger over data centers, the large facilities that house the computers powering AI, is becoming a political force. With Democrats now in control of Congress, that could lead to new limits on where data centers can be built and how much say local communities have. Data centers became a ballot-box issue in various states. An NBC exit poll showed how concerned voters are about AI: More than half of respondents believe that AI will do more harm than good, while almost 80% are against the building of data centers in their neighborhoods. Almost 60%, meanwhile, said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote. Nadine Smith, president and CEO of the racial justice organization Color of Change, called Tuesday’s election a referendum on “who this economy is built for.” “National security matters,” Smith said, referring to a common argument from data center supporters that the infrastructure is essential for the U.S. to stay ahead in war and in its rivalry with China. “And so do the families in South Memphis breathing exhaust from the gas turbines powering an AI supercomputer.” (She was referring to xAI’s data center in Memphis, Tennessee, which uses gas turbines for power.) Voters in several states pushed back against the AI buildout, even as pro-AI super PACs spent millions hoping to sway them this midterm. The anti-data center backlash was especially felt in states like Ohio, where OpenAI has eyed a $500 billion data center, backed by more than $100 billion in financing from Nvidia. In fact, the Ohio county where Meta had planned a 700,000-square-foot facility just passed a ban on data centers, and local communities across the state overwhelmingly voted against data center buildout measures. Analysts at Morgan Stanley predict that Democratic governor-elect Amy Acton will also pose a major risk to Ohio’s data center buildout. Elsewhere, candidates in Texas, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Georgia, and South Carolina all won seats after taking a stance against the rapid buildout of data centers. “It is clear that money does not buy outcomes,” said Anshi Bhatt, a tech and policy researcher, adding that in modern politics, creating a “local villain” is one way to build campaign momentum. Likely next steps include more construction moratoriums or requiring data centers to pay for their own power grid upgrades instead of passing those costs on to nearby communities. Goldman Sachs, in fact, predicts data center construction delays in states like Georgia and Texas because of Democratic gains. Democratic control of Congress could also improve the odds for bills like the one Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced earlier this year, though any such bill would also face a possible veto. It proposes a nationwide moratorium on new data centers until Congress adds new guardrails and ensures that the buildout does not raise electricity costs, harm the environment, or proceed without community approval. There are also bills like the GRID Savings Act, proposed by New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich, which would prevent grid infrastructure costs from being passed on to communities during large AI data center buildouts. The environment is also a major concern, especially at xAI’s data center in Memphis and at the data centers throughout Virginia, known as the world capital of data centers, where gas turbines are used for power. Maia Woluchem, program director at Data & Society, a nonprofit research group, believes that changes to energy regulations, land rights, and other environmental policies could affect the data center buildout, especially as congressional Democrats look further into the Trump administration’s rollback of certain energy protections, as the New York Times reported they might . “Regardless of federal action, I could imagine that we will see additional movement at the state and local level, given the momentum that’s been building from the ground up,” Woluchem continued, citing governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who supports a statewide moratorium on data centers, as an example. Both Hinojosa and Gov. Greg Abbott called for some limits, but Hinojosa centered much of her campaign on opposing data centers, a notable choice in Texas, whose electrical grid has proved vulnerable over the past decade. But the hard part is still to come. Smith, for example, is now expecting a fight, or even more executive orders, to bypass what Congress is now likely to block. “Even among Democrats, a blanket freeze is contested,” she said, referring to some Democrats’ worry that a moratorium could slow AI progress and hurt national security.

articles.title: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here's how they fared | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI industry PACs spent millions influencing the 2026 midterms, with mixed results. Political groups are already looking toward the next election cycle.
articles.body_text: Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races. On the industry side, two AI-focused political action committees (PACs) that raised and spent money to influence the elections — American Mission and Building the Future — collectively spent $4.8 million to back South Carolina Senate candidate Darline Graham, who lost. American Mission is the Republican spending arm of Leading the Future (LTF), a broader political group backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and the VC firm Andreessen Horowitz. American Mission also spent more than $500,000 apiece supporting Republican House candidates Aaron Flint in Montana and Laurie Buckhout in North Carolina, both of whom lost. LTF’s Democratic spending arm, Think Big, had better luck backing Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who won reelection. Groups advocating for stronger AI safeguards also saw mixed results. Public First, which is backed by Anthropic, supported several Republicans who lost through its affiliated PAC but had more success backing Democratic candidates. It also contributed $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener, who was leading his race at the time of publication. Meanwhile, Guardrails Alliance , a group that has sought to make taking money from AI companies a political liability, spent more than $1 million apiece opposing two candidates who lost: California Rep. Jimmy Gomez and Montana’s Aaron Flint. It also spent $300,000 supporting Angela Gonzales-Torres, who defeated Gomez. It’s difficult to separate the impact of AI-related spending from the broader Democratic wave that swept Tuesday’s elections. Elon Musk, who reportedly poured half a billion dollars into supporting Republicans in the midterms, also saw many of his candidates lose . Indeed, LTF also backed some candidates it believed were likely to win, only to see them lose to the Dems. For LTF, though, the general election wasn’t the main focus. The group told TechCrunch ahead of Election Day that it thinks primaries (the contests that choose each party’s nominee) are a more effective use of its money, because spending there can build name recognition and help candidates set up AI policy agendas. LTF spent $27.38 million in the primaries, including $8 million alone on opposing New York Assembly member Alex Bores , who lost his bid for Congress back in June. When deciding whether it’s worth jumping into a general election race, LTF assesses how competitive the race is, whether it thinks spending could make a difference, and whether it should keep its powder dry for future elections. Charlie Blaettler, political director of Guardrails Alliance, had a different theory for why LTF spent comparatively little in the general election. “They don’t want their money to become an issue in these elections,” he said. He pointed to the Michigan Senate primary election, in which a pro-Israel lobbying group called AIPAC spent close to $30 million backing Democratic candidate Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens conceded the primary to El-Sayed, who went on to win the Senate seat. “AIPAC became the story in that race,” Blaettler said. “We know people hate AI billionaires. They hate the people running these companies. They’re very distrustful and disgusted by the political spending and lobbying that the tech industry does. If they spend in a competitive race, they would just become an enormous liability for their candidates.” The main fight among AI-related PACs, whether they are pro-industry or pro-regulation, is whether Congress should establish a national AI framework that overrides state laws , or whether states will maintain their own ability to impose safeguards.

articles.title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says | TechCrunch
articles.summary: During its busiest week last quarter, Uber said only four people booked a ride using an AI agent.
articles.body_text: Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween. While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips. Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent. “It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.” The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf. There’s been an explosion of personal AI startups, including one of the buzziest, Instinct, which was founded last year and raised its most recent round of funding at a $10 billion valuation. Meta’s Muse also became the No. 1 app in Apple’s U.S. App Store last month, topping 10 million users, per Meta’s own reporting . The company said many were using it to shop and transact with businesses. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (Grok) are also now offering their own AI agents, as are numerous smaller startups. Still, early numbers from public companies indicate the agentic web still has a long way to go. DoorDash, for instance, said last week on its earnings call that it has only received a few hundred orders from AI agents so far, as most customers are still placing orders through the DoorDash app. Uber is seeing the same behavior, it seems. Khosrowshahi pointed out that the average time to book a ride is only 50 seconds in the company’s app, and re-ordering a favorite food only takes 90 seconds. That suggests an AI agent isn’t necessarily saving anyone time. Despite the low number of AI-driven transactions, Khosrowshahi seemed bullish on the idea of agents in general. “We think that is another opportunity to reach our platform. We think it will be a net positive in terms of demand on the ecosystem,” he said. Right now, there are around eight major AI assistants on the market, Khosrowshahi noted, and he expects that number to grow to more than 10 in time. “Every single AI system company is talking to us,” he added. articles.title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane wants AI to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing the AI giant’s own business interests.
articles.body_text: OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane thinks the 2028 presidential election could be a defining moment for AI. And he wants politicians to start developing policies that address Americans’ concerns about the technology, rather than simply paying lip service to anti-AI sentiment and the backlash against data centers . In a new essay , Lehane compares AI’s potential to reshape the economy to President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal, the 1930s set of federal programs and reforms enacted after industrialization and the Great Depression shattered the old economic order. He observes that Americans today feel similarly anxious about losing control over their economic futures and urges politicians to find a “compelling third path” that allows people to share in AI’s benefits. He lays out five policy priorities, spanning worker protections and education to AI safety and data center development. The essay comes on the heels of a stunning Democratic victory in the midterm elections, in which Democrats flipped control of Congress amid widespread voter frustration over the cost of living. Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that Lehane’s rhetoric marks a notable shift from OpenAI’s policy agenda last year, which focused on accelerating AI development, reducing regulatory barriers, and expanding infrastructure. Unsurprisingly, many of Lehane’s proposals would encourage wider AI adoption and support the infrastructure expansion companies like OpenAI need to grow. The original New Deal established protections for workers and placed constraints on corporate power. It’s less clear how Lehane’s vision would hold AI companies accountable for the economic disruption their technology could create. “Invoking a New Deal metaphor is to invoke state capacity to actually benefit the public,” Brennan said. “This is written by a private company that is trying to advocate for policies for its own benefit. It is ahistorical at best and harmful at worst.” While AI wasn’t a dominant issue in the midterms, opposition to data centers emerged as a major bipartisan concern in several races in the midterms. And Lehane may be right that AI will become a bigger part of the conversation over the next two years. Affordability is already shaping up as a key issue for the 2028 election as Americans grapple with inflation, tariffs, and the rising cost of living. AI could become an increasingly large part of that conversation as voters stress about data centers hiking up electricity bills, AI replacing their jobs, and technology’s economic gains flowing only to a handful of wealthy companies. Lehane acknowledges many of these concerns, but he offers few concrete proposals to prevent AI’s gains from becoming concentrated. Instead, he largely pitches AI as a path to greater prosperity for Americans willing to embrace it. Take his proposals for the tax code. He suggests incentives for workers to learn AI skills, easier capital access for entrepreneurs, and new approaches to employee ownership and profit-sharing. Those are not the same as binding requirements that would ensure workers share in AI-generated wealth or that companies pay the costs of displacing workers. “I was struck by how much of this policy is for a future…that is already predicated on mass AI adoption and AI benefiting society, which we have yet to see,” Brennan said. “All of it is predicated on benefiting from AI’s upside.” Brennan said it would make more sense to see things like a revised corporate tax rate or tax incentives for hiring human beings rather than automating jobs, as well as ways to keep companies from amassing outsize market power. Lehane’s emphasis on expanding AI’s economic opportunities, rather than limiting potential harms, extends to data centers. He notes concerns about data centers while emphasizing the construction jobs and local tax revenue they could generate. He then warns that politicians who support a data center moratorium could jeopardize America’s lead over China, going so far as to compare that stance to the 2002 vote to authorize the Iraq war.

articles.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The startup allows software engineers to deploy teams of agents to work on various aspects of a project simultaneously.
articles.body_text: Meta has acquired Conductor , an AI coding startup that allows users to spin up software projects by deploying multiple agents into parallel workspaces. The news was originally reported by Axios, and Conductor shared news of its acquisition on its blog. “I have big news: Conductor is joining Meta,” wrote the startup’s founder and CEO, Charlie Holtz, on Wednesday. “We have some big, crazy plans for the next interface,” he added, teasing that the company would have “something new” for customers to use by “early next year.” On X, Holtz also noted that he was looking forward to working with Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, and Nat Friedman, head of product at the company’s Superintelligence Labs. “They’ve been on an absolute tear, and I’m convinced MSL has the highest talent density of all the labs,” he added. Meta confirmed the acquisition to TechCrunch but wouldn’t comment further or provide additional details about the deal. Conductor, founded in 2024, only launched its core product just last summer. The company’s agentic teams, which can be deployed in the cloud, locally, or via a user’s phone, are designed to help software engineers work on separate, compartmentalized parts of a project in concert. The agents that the platform deploys aren’t developed in-house but come from major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Holtz said that, until early next year, Conductor’s core features would continue to work as they previously have. The exception is Conductor’s cloud service, which will shut down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting user cloud data. Meta, which previously lagged behind in AI services, has spent the last several months trying to catch up. In August, the company launched Muse Code , its own coding agent. Meanwhile, the company’s recently launched Muse agents are seeing significant adoption, with the company recently reporting that the service had surpassed 10 million users. The company has also made a number of AI-related acquisitions over the past year, including Moltbook , the viral agent platform that made headlines. articles.title: DuckDuckGo pitches itself to schools amid backlash over Google's AI policy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: DuckDuckGo is courting schools frustrated by Google's AI restrictions, pointing educators to its search engine and options to disable AI features.
articles.body_text: DuckDuckGo is pitching itself to schools after Google created an opening for the alternative search engine. On Tuesday, Google told schools they could turn off Gemini , but it said shutting off its other AI features would cost schools Google Search , as well. On X , DuckDuckGo’s founder and CEO, Gabriel Weinberg, pointed to the company’s online documentation , explaining how schools can switch their default search engine to DuckDuckGo’s service instead, adding, “get in touch for help.” Meanwhile, DuckDuckGo’s chief public affairs officer, Kamyl Bazbaz, issued a stronger statement, writing , “Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless. Prove Google wrong.” Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless. Prove Google wrong. https://t.co/Ta6ibmFdb9 In an email to TechCrunch, DuckDuckGo chastised Google for its decision, adding that Google could easily turn off Search’s AI features for schools if it wanted to. The company’s comments come as the American public is weighing how much AI they want to allow into their lives. As Tuesday night’s elections indicate, they don’t want AI data centers built in their towns. But using AI at work and school has become a common practice and requires a more nuanced discussion. Knowing that educators have struggled with AI, Google developed technology called “ Guided Learning ” that is meant to help kids learn by walking through problem-solving steps rather than just providing them with an answer. But educators are still asking for tools that let them remove AI from the learning process altogether. After the backlash on Tuesday, Google defended its decision, saying it was just responding to schools’ feedback. It said that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search would be off by default, and schools could choose to enable them individually. We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced: – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default. This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control… The problem, of course, is that Google Search now heavily uses AI, through AI Overviews and a conversational AI Mode that answers users’ queries. DuckDuckGo isn’t anti-AI, to be clear — it offers its own set of AI features, including a chat interface called Duck.ai and an AI search assistant. However, unlike Google, it provides options to disable these features in both its search and browser settings, the company says. It also offers a dedicated website, noai.duckduckgo.com , where AI-assisted answers, AI-generated images, and AI feature suggestions are all turned off.

articles.title: 'You Can See Everything' is getting an outer space release and it hasn't even come out in Europe yet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: It is easier to watch the Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything" in low Earth orbit than in London.
articles.body_text: The film company behind the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything ,” A24, posted on Instagram that it granted a request from NASA to screen the film on the International Space Station (ISS). Unless A24 is deceiving us ( why would they? ), it appears that some astronauts can’t wait to come back to Earth to see the film that everyone’s talking about, which has reached number one at the box office. “You Can See Everything,” directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, initially debuted in North America with a limited theatrical rollout. The film has been so successful, though, that it’s generating demand from international audiences. The film won’t come out in the U.K. until November 20, while French viewers will have to wait until December 30. So yes, it is currently easier to watch “You Can See Everything” in low Earth orbit than in London. These hard-working astronauts can take a break from their complex scientific research to address an equally bewildering question: Does Elizabeth Holmes really believe her own lies? articles.title: Sequoia hits rewind, undoing 20 years of expansion | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sequoia is consolidating into a smaller, Bay Area–centered firm, shutting down the programs and offices it built during a 20-year expansion while announcing roughly $10 billion in new funds.
articles.body_text: Sequoia Capital posted a memo to X on Wednesday morning titled “The Sequoia of Tomorrow” that’s full of surprises. The firm has raised roughly $10 billion in new funds, it says. It is also closing its London office, shutting down its Arc accelerator and its Scouts program, merging its early-stage and growth teams into one, flattening its partnership, and killing the Monday partner meeting. The framing is forward-looking, but the messaging is very much about rewinding to an earlier time when the team was smaller and focused more narrowly on Silicon Valley. Sequoia says as much itself. The firm describes coming out of a roughly 20-year expansionary phase during which it built multiple businesses in multiple geographies and says an unintended side effect was hierarchy. Nearly everything being undone here was built during that stretch, under a succession of stewards running from Doug Leone to Jim Goetz to Roelof Botha. One of the most surprising developments is that the firm is killing two programs that put Sequoia closest to young founders. Scouts , which Sequoia launched around 2009 and, anecdotally, half the industry has since copied in some form, gave small checks to founders and operators to invest on the firm’s behalf; it was a way to see deals through people closer to interesting new founders than any partner could be. Jason Calacanis famously pointed Sequoia to Uber through the program. Sam Altman brought Stripe to Sequoia as a scout, too. Other early scouts included Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky and Dropbox founders Arash Ferdowsi and Drew Houston. Arc , launched in March 2022, was Sequoia’s answer to Y Combinator: a batch accelerator for pre-seed and seed founders, running several cohorts a year for seven weeks, with admitted companies getting $500,000 to $1 million up front. Both were bets on being early and being everywhere. Now Sequoia says it wants to put more energy behind fewer people and things. Also gone is the firm’s London office, which Sequoia opened in 2020. Several people will leave the firm as result. “We simply don’t see the need for a local presence,” the memo says, adding that Europe will keep producing “outlier founders” and that Sequoia can support them from the Bay Area. (If founders didn’t already feel pressured to move to the Bay Area or open an office in the region, they will now.) Luciana Lixandru, hired from Accel in 2020 as Sequoia’s first partner in Europe, says she was offered a move to San Francisco and declined. (“Europe is where my family is, and where I want to build,” she wrote on X.) She says she remains a partner and will keep her board seats while investing personally in European founders. For European entrepreneurs, the message is going to be particularly difficult to digest, especially as it follows Andreessen Horowitz shuttering its London office last year and Coatue closing its own in 2024. Sequoia didn’t say it won’t fund Europeans, but it’s definitely reinforcing here that the center of gravity is once again in the Bay Area. The rewind extends to people, too. The memo notes that Carl Eschenbach, the former Workday CEO, is very much back in the fold (he returned as a full-time partner in March). It also says the team has “reinvigorated the GOAT,” Doug Leone. Though the nomenclature at venture firms is all over the place — including Sequoia — the memo makes clear there are now seven general partners who primarily own and operate Sequoia: Alfred Lin and Pat Grady — who are the firm’s co-stewards — along with Andrew Reed, Shaun Maguire, Konstantine Buhler, Sonya Huang, and David Cahn, who joined the firm in 2023. There are other changes as a result. Jess Lee, the firm’s first female partner and an early-stage investor who oversaw its Arc program, is no longer shown on Sequoia’s investor page but rather as an operator in the role of its chief product officer. Stephanie Zhan, an investor who had joined Sequoia in 2015, has meanwhile left the firm entirely, announcing last month that she is launching her own new firm.

articles.title: I tried Apple's Siri Recaps. They're surprisingly useful — and a little unsettling | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple's AI-powered Siri Recaps won me over in just one day, despite my privacy reservations. But there's still room for improvement.
articles.body_text: On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The betas bring four new AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes. After just a day with Apple’s Siri Recaps feature on my Apple Watch, I can already see how its value may ultimately outweigh any creepiness factor that comes from the AI-powered audio recording and summarization it provides. However, I also see areas where AI-assisted note-taking can go too far, capturing things that aren’t worth remembering, and where there’s room for improvement. It’s the two other features, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps, that have raised concerns. The features record and then transcribe or summarize the conversations happening with and around the Apple Watch’s owner. Live Rewind lets you go back to see what was said in the past 15 seconds, while Siri Recaps summarize audio throughout your day, saving notes of the important things that were said. Still, some are put off by the idea that we’re now normalizing the idea that technology is always listening . I find myself sympathizing with both camps. I often lament that we’ve allowed technology to become so pervasive in our daily lives, but I still see the value in what Apple has built. I haven’t yet had an appropriate time to test Live Rewind, nor do I think this will be a feature I use as often. I’m more likely to say “sorry, what?” or “can you repeat that?” if I missed something that was said, before turning to my Apple Watch for help. But with Siri Recaps, I immediately saw how this could become a feature I rely on regularly to save important notes for later. I was able to test the feature in a real-world scenario yesterday, when we were dropping off my teen’s car for repairs and picking up a rental. At both places, employees shared a lot of information about time frames, prices, and policies that were delivered verbally. The information came too fast to stop and write anything down. Yet when I returned to Siri Recaps later in the day, it had captured key details that I may need to refer back to. For instance, it noted the deductible, the repair time frame, the amount of gas we had in the rental at the start, and other things I wanted to remember. One complaint is that Siri Recaps had mixed this information with other topics that were later discussed in the home, like an errand we needed to run and what time babysitting was this week, something we were discussing in order to create an appointment on the family calendar with an appropriate alert time frame. I think these items should have been saved in a separate note titled “family schedule and errands,” rather than in the same note with the car repairs, but under a separate heading. Because I configured Siri Recaps to run at all times, it also captured non-essential things, like our “plan” to watch the midterms coverage on TV, which is not the kind of thing you’d normally jot down a note about. It also was a stark reminder that the feature was listening in on our everyday conversations. That’s something that could feel invasive in different scenarios, if the subject being discussed was more personal in nature.
